declaration.goal: Crawl ahead by 0.3 to 0.5 m, keeping within 0.2 m of the start line and within 20 degrees of the start heading.
declaration.measured_by: Computed from the simulator's pose, as the quantities a camera straight above could measure; not measured from a camera image. The camera sees a floor area of 2.59 m by 1.46 m. x, y and heading are relative to the start of each trial: x in the direction the body faces at the start, y to its left, heading counter-clockwise seen from above, in (-180, 180]. At the start the body is at x = 0, y = 0, and the view spans x from -0.84 to 1.74 m and y from -0.73 to 0.73 m. A value is lost when the camera could not see the tracked point.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c1 is held at -0.5 and c3 is a unit sine at 1.5 Hz with the other inputs at 0, THE system SHALL end at x between 0.3 and 0.5 m with heading within 20 deg of the start.

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Half-strength c1 with a c3 sine at 1.5 Hz crawls 0.3 to 0.5 m and stays straight

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Half-strength c1 with a c3 sine at 1.5 Hz crawls 0.3 to 0.5 m and stays straight

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: With c1=-0.5 held and a unit c3 sine, x was -0.055 (f=2), -0.028 (f=1), -0.023 (f=1.5); heading -7.7, -1.2, -1.2 deg. The body barely moved. Both P1 (x 0.3-0.5) and P2 hit/miss moot: P1 missed. P2 hit only because nothing moved. This contradicts given R9/R11 (c1=-0.5 alone should give x +0.06 and heading -19; with c3 sine x 0.26 at f=1). The c1 constant seems to have no effect here.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c1 is held at -1 and c3 is a unit sine at 1.5 Hz with the other inputs at 0, THE system SHALL end at x between 0.4 and 0.55 m, as E9 reported (0.469); and WHEN c1 is -1 with c3 at 0, THE system SHALL end at x between 0.08 and 0.15 m.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: Neither given result replicated. c1=-1 alone: x 2.5e-5, heading -0.004, only a decaying transient (given R9 predicted x 0.115, heading -37). c1=-1 with unit c3 sine at 1.5 Hz: x -0.023, heading -1.2 (given E9: x 0.469, heading -29). P1 and P2 both missed. The channels may be permuted or the system changed relative to given/.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN all five inputs are held at 1, THE system SHALL show steady motion, so that |x| exceeds 0.1 m or |heading| exceeds 5 deg at the end.

title.text: Some channel still drives steady motion when held constant

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: All five inputs held at 1: x -0.009, y -0.011, heading -12.6, all settled within 0.1 s, then no motion. P1 missed (x not below -0.1). No channel gives steady motion when held at +1, so the given c1 drift is absent.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN channel i is sin(2*pi*1.5*t - 1.0*i) for i = 0..4, THE system SHALL end at x between 0.1 and 0.4 m with heading within 40 deg of the start, as E5 suggested (x 0.219 at f = 1.5).

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: Wave f=1.5, ph=1.0 (lag per channel index) gave x -0.080, y 0.076, heading -146 deg, rotating steadily at about 30 deg/s. P1 missed (x 0.1-0.4) and P2 missed (heading within 40 deg). Matches given R5 (wave mostly rotates), not the given E5 x 0.219.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN all five inputs are 1.5 Hz unit sines with lag ph per channel, THE system SHALL end with x between 0.3 and 0.5 m and heading within 20 deg for at least one of ph = 0, 2, -1 (here stated for ph = -1).

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: A wave with a different phase lag moves the body forward without rotating it

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: A wave with a different phase lag moves the body forward without rotating it

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: At f=1.5, ph=0: x -0.088, heading -153. ph=2: x -0.018, heading +61. ph=-1 (P1): x -0.038, y 0.144, heading +55. P1 missed. No ph gave forward travel. Heading rotation is monotone from -146 at ph=1 to +60 at ph=2, so heading near 0 may be near ph 1.7, but x stays within 0.1 m.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN all five inputs are 1.5 Hz unit sines with lag ph = 1.7 rad per channel, THE system SHALL end with heading within 20 deg of the start, because heading falls from -146 at ph 1 to +61 at ph 2.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: P1 (heading within 20 deg at f=1.5, ph=1.7) missed: heading +43.3, x 0.006, y 0.057. At f=3, ph=1.7 the body travelled forward: x 0.391, y 0.162, heading +29.1. That meets the x and y limits but not the 20 deg heading limit. It was run first in the compare, so the last trial (the answer) is the f=1.5 one, which misses the goal. Budget is exhausted.
